context: The prompt requests to add delete functionality for execution mode outputs (Clarify/questionnaire, Analyze/analysis, Plan/plan files). The functionality should include both UI buttons with trash bin icons and corresponding backend scripts. The scripts should delete the respective files and reset the status flags as if the execution mode was never executed.

questions.question-text: When deleting a questionnaire file, should the questionnaire-answered flag also be reset to false, or should it remain unchanged?

options.label: Reset both questionnaire-generated and questionnaire-answered flags to false
options.pros: Complete reset - treats it as if the questionnaire was never executed. Ensures consistency - if the questionnaire doesn't exist, it can't have been answered. Clean state for regeneration.
options.cons: Loses information that the questionnaire was previously answered. User would need to answer again if questionnaire is regenerated.

options.label: Reset only questionnaire-generated flag to false, leave questionnaire-answered unchanged
options.pros: Preserves information that user had interacted with questionnaire. Could be useful for tracking historical engagement.
options.cons: Creates inconsistent state - questionnaire-answered=true but questionnaire-generated=false is illogical. May confuse downstream logic that expects answered implies generated.

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A provides a complete and consistent reset. Since the file will be deleted, there's no meaningful way for questionnaire-answered to be true without questionnaire-generated also being true. This matches the behavior of 'as if the execution-mode was never executed' mentioned in the prompt.

questions.question-text: Should the delete scripts support deleting files for any prompt (via prompt-id parameter), or only for the active prompt?

options.label: Support both - accept optional prompt-id parameter, default to active prompt if not provided
options.pros: Maximum flexibility - can delete files from historical prompts. Consistent with existing scripts like prompt_questionnaire_generated_off.py. Useful for cleanup operations.
options.cons: Slightly more complex implementation. Need to handle error cases when prompt-id doesn't exist.

options.label: Only support active prompt - no prompt-id parameter
options.pros: Simpler implementation. Focuses on current work context. Reduces risk of accidentally modifying historical prompts.
options.cons: Less flexible - can't cleanup files from completed prompts. User would need to manually delete files from historical prompts.

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A is consistent with the existing pattern in the codebase (e.g., prompt_questionnaire_generated_off.py supports optional prompt-id). This provides flexibility while maintaining a sensible default behavior, and allows the UI to potentially call these scripts for any prompt, not just the active one.

questions.question-text: Where should the trash bin delete buttons be placed in the UI cards for execution modes?

options.label: In the header area of each execution mode card, aligned to the right of the card title
options.pros: Clear visual association with the specific execution mode. Easy to find. Standard UI pattern for delete actions.
options.cons: Takes up space in the card header. Multiple buttons in header might look cluttered.

options.label: In the file view area, next to the file name when the respective file is displayed
options.pros: Direct visual association with the file being deleted. Only visible when file is shown. Cleaner card headers.
options.cons: Less discoverable - user needs to open file view to see delete option. Different location than execution mode radio buttons.

options.label: Next to the status icon for each execution mode
options.pros: Groups all execution mode controls in one visual area. Clear association between status and delete action. Compact layout.
options.cons: Could be visually crowded if status icon, file button, execution mode radio, and delete button are all together.

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt mentions 'buttons with icon trash bin in the respective cards for execution-modes' and references the existing visual grouping of 'status icon, file button, and radio for execution-mode setting'. Placing the delete button next to the status icon keeps all execution mode controls together in the same visual area, which aligns with the current design pattern where these elements are grouped.

questions.question-text: Should the delete buttons be enabled/disabled based on the file existence and status flags?

options.label: Enable only when the respective generated flag is true (questionnaire-generated, analysis-generated, plan-generated)
options.pros: Prevents attempting to delete files that don't exist. Clear visual indicator of what can be deleted. Consistent with the file view buttons pattern.
options.cons: Doesn't handle case where file was manually deleted but flag is still true. Less resilient to inconsistent states.

options.label: Always enabled - let the script handle the case when file doesn't exist
options.pros: Simpler UI logic. Script can provide appropriate error message if file doesn't exist. User can clean up inconsistent states.
options.cons: User might click delete button when there's nothing to delete. Could be confusing.

options.label: Enable when either the file exists OR the generated flag is true
options.pros: Handles both normal case and inconsistent states. Allows cleanup when file is missing but flag is set, or vice versa. Most robust approach.
options.cons: More complex UI logic - needs to check both file existence and registry flags. May perform unnecessary file system checks.

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A is consistent with the existing pattern for file view buttons which are 'disabled when the statuses are not true'. This provides clear visual feedback and prevents unnecessary API calls. The scripts can handle edge cases gracefully if needed (e.g., file missing but flag is true).

questions.question-text: When deleting the plan file, should the plan-generated flag be reset to false in addition to deleting the file?

options.label: Yes, reset plan-generated to false
options.pros: Consistent with the approach for questionnaire and analysis. Matches the requirement of toggling status 'as if the execution-mode was never executed'. Clean state.
options.cons: None significant - this is the expected behavior based on the prompt.

options.label: No, only delete the file but keep plan-generated as true
options.pros: Preserves historical information that plan was generated at some point.
options.cons: Inconsistent state - plan-generated=true but file doesn't exist. Violates the prompt requirement to reset status.

questions.recommendation-rationale: The prompt explicitly states to 'toggle the status - as if the execution-mode was never executed'. This clearly indicates that the generated flag should be reset to false, maintaining consistency across all three execution modes (Clarify, Analyze, Plan).

questions.question-text: Should there be a confirmation dialog before deleting execution mode files, or should the delete action be immediate?

options.label: Show confirmation dialog with warning message before deleting
options.pros: Prevents accidental deletions. Gives user chance to reconsider. Standard pattern for destructive operations. User-friendly.
options.cons: Extra step - could slow down workflow. More UI implementation work.

options.label: Delete immediately without confirmation
options.pros: Faster workflow. Simpler implementation. User can regenerate files if needed.
options.cons: Risk of accidental deletions. No undo functionality. Could frustrate users who delete by mistake.

options.label: Create backup before deleting (following UR-0028 requirement) but no confirmation dialog
options.pros: Allows recovery if deletion was mistake. Meets framework requirement for backups. No workflow interruption with dialogs.
options.cons: More complex implementation. Backup management overhead. User might not know backups exist.

questions.recommendation-rationale: Option A follows best practices for destructive operations and prevents user frustration from accidental deletions. While requirement UR-0028 mentions backups, a confirmation dialog is simpler, more intuitive, and sufficient for this use case since the files can be regenerated. The dialog can be a simple 'Are you sure you want to delete the [questionnaire/analysis/plan] file?' prompt.
